# Round 3 review prompt for GPT

This file has two parts. Part 1 is for the sender: which file to attach and how to send it. Part 2 is the prompt, to be copied verbatim from the line "PROMPT START" to "PROMPT END" and pasted into the ChatGPT chat box.

Round 3 is the last review round before the document set is locked as the baseline for Discovery. Goals:

- Check whether the 24 round 2 proposals (RF2-01 to RF2-24) were handled correctly.
- Assess the two new parts since 3/10/2026:
  - the process framework editor in the main BRD version 4.4;
  - the BRD addendum "Onboarding in 30 minutes" version 1.0 with its 12 wireframes.
- Check that the two documents match each other.

The onboarding design is the number one focus: it is the key feature, and it must be easy to understand, friendly, scientifically grounded and appealing to users. The prompt keeps the product owner's constraint: do not propose cutting or postponing scope because of team size.

## Part 1. Sending instructions

### Send one message

1. Open a new conversation in ChatGPT. The round 2 report is already in the zip, so there is no need to continue the old conversation.
2. Choose a model with a deep reasoning mode if your plan has one; turn on the code execution tool, because GPT needs it to unzip the zip.
3. Paste the prompt from Part 2 into the chat box.
4. Attach `review/metis-review-pack-round3.zip` (about 22 MB, 85 files).
5. Send.

This is the only pack that needs to be sent: it already contains the BRD addendum on onboarding together with its spec, option catalogue, research notes and wireframes.

### What is in the zip file

Every file is in the folder `metis-review-pack-round3/`:

- `Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_v4.4.md`: the main BRD version 4.4, the primary source.
- `Enterprise_Portfolio_Intelligence_Governance_Platform_BRD_Addendum_Onboarding_v1.0.md`: the BRD addendum on onboarding, version 1.0.
- `wireframes-digest.md`: the text and annotations of the 58 wireframes.
- `manifest.json`: maps screens to the requirement IDs of both documents.
- `png/`: the 58 wireframes as images (01 to 45 and 58 belong to the main BRD, 46 to 57 belong to the BRD addendum).
- `style-guide.md`, `style-guide.png`, `tokens.css`: style guide 0.3.
- `round-2/metis-review-vong-2.md`: GPT's round 2 report; `round-2/review-disposition-round2.md`: how the team handled each round 2 item.
- `poc-frameworks/poc-frameworks-coverage.md` and `poc-frameworks/evidence/`: the survey of the POC's Frameworks menu on 3/10/2026, with 10 screenshots and the export data; the basis of the process framework editor part.
- `onboarding/design/`: the onboarding design spec, the option catalogue and the rulings made during execution; `onboarding/research/`: three market research notes with URLs and dates.

Not in the zip because they are not needed: the .docx files, the original POC images, the wireframe HTML files. The BRD already contains the POC evidence; the digest file already contains the text of the HTML.

### If GPT reports that it cannot view the images in the zip

In round 1 and round 2, GPT opened and viewed all the images in the zip, so this time it will most likely work too. If not, also send the images directly into the chat window, giving priority to these screens:

- `46-onboarding-frame`, `47-onboarding-reading`, `48-onboarding-draft-cockpit`, `49-onboarding-approval-flow`;
- `50-onboarding-questions`, `51-onboarding-adoption`, `52-onboarding-launch`, `53-onboarding-owner-tasks`;
- `58-process-framework-editor`, `13-template-library`.

The OpenAI user forum reports that each message accepts at most 10 files; this figure is not yet in the official FAQ [Unverified - confirm before applying].

The official limits according to the OpenAI File Uploads FAQ (help.openai.com/en/articles/8555545), as recorded in round 1: at most 512 MB per file, 20 MB per image, 80 files per 3 hours.

When you receive the result, save the Markdown file that GPT returns as `metis/review/metis-review-vong-3.md`.

## Part 2. Prompt

---- PROMPT START ----

# Role

You are the independent review panel that reviewed the previous two rounds of this project. This round the panel has four experts working as one team:

1. A business analyst and PMO expert with many years working on project portfolio management (PPM) software and B2B SaaS.
2. A UX lead for enterprise software, specializing in onboarding, first-time experience and the experience for C-level executives; well versed in research on user behavior.
3. A solution architect for multi-tenant SaaS and LLM integration through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
4. An AI application security expert: prompt injection, data leakage, the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications.

Round 3 is the last round before the document set is locked as the baseline for Discovery. Task: check the round 2 remediation, assess the two new parts, check that the two documents match each other, and give the final conclusion. Critique, do not praise. Every remark must be specific, backed by evidence, and come with a proposal that can be carried out.

**The number one focus of this round is the onboarding design (part O).** The product owner regards onboarding as the key feature of Metis: customers judge the product by the first 30 minutes. The design must be easy to understand, friendly, scientifically grounded and appealing to users. Give part O the greatest thoroughness and the largest share of the report.

# Context

- **Product:** "Metis" (working name), Enterprise Portfolio Intelligence & Governance Platform, multi-tenant SaaS, with an MCP server for LLMs.
- **Round 2** (02/10/2026): the report `round-2/metis-review-vong-2.md` concluded "Go with conditions".
  - The 54 round 1 proposals comprise 39 closed, 11 partly closed, 1 not closed and 3 where a new defect arose.
  - Plus 24 new proposals, RF2-01 to RF2-24.
  - The team handled each item in `round-2/review-disposition-round2.md` (Vietnamese) and applied it to BRD version 4.3 (section 1.8 of BRD 4.4).
- **Since 03/10/2026 there are two new parts.**
  1. **Process framework editor** (main BRD version 4.4, section 1.9). This is the result of the survey of the POC's Settings, Frameworks menu (`poc-frameworks/`; the survey was done on version 4.3, and section 8 of that file lists what was applied). This part consists of:
     - four new P0 requirements: BLD-13 (the process framework authoring screen), BLD-14 (node template), BLD-15 (typed links with lag), BLD-16 (lifecycle of draft, publish and deprecation in Release 1);
     - D-09 updated with five decisions of the product owner;
     - new wireframe `58-process-framework-editor`; revised `13-template-library` and `36-workspace-setup`.
  2. **The BRD addendum "Onboarding in 30 minutes" version 1.0**, a separate document. Contents:
     - module M23 with 40 requirements prefixed ONB (27 P0, 13 P1);
     - 8 rules BR-43 to BR-50, 8 decisions D-32 to D-39, 5 questions Q-14 to Q-18;
     - assumptions A-08 to A-10, sources S7 to S13, wireframes 46 to 57.

     Section 13 of the BRD addendum lists 20 amendments proposed to the main BRD; these amendments are not yet merged into version 4.4 and wait for the result of this round. The BRD addendum was drafted on version 4.3, then its base was switched to 4.4 on the same day. The team cross-checked every line of section 13 against version 4.4 again.
- **The ID scheme and the automated build.** The two documents share one ID scheme. The automated build checks:
  - IDs are not duplicated;
  - every reference exists in one of the two documents;
  - every P0 requirement has at least one wireframe.

  The main BRD build skips the screens that carry ONB IDs; the BRD addendum build checks the 12 onboarding screens against the IDs of both documents. Check this again yourself with `manifest.json`, and judge whether a screen really shows the behavior or only lists the ID.
- **The product owner's constraints, which must be followed:**
  - Development capacity is an agency of about 40 developers working in parallel (assumption A-07, section 5.3 of the main BRD). Do not propose cutting or postponing scope because of team size. You may still propose changing scope for other reasons (value to users, technical risk, dependencies, legal); in that case state the reason clearly.
  - Onboarding (section 1.2 of the BRD addendum):
    - the main setup person is a C-level executive with very little time;
    - the questions for the executive are asked from the executive's point of view and contain no preset numbers;
    - Metis does not build or train a model itself: Metis calls a third-party LLM through an API that the customer turns on, and that AI uses Metis's own MCP to create records;
    - the data belongs to the customer, and security focuses on the boundary;
    - there is a path that uses the customer's own AI and a path that uses no AI.
  - Process framework (D-09 of the main BRD):
    - in Release 1, publishing needs no review step;
    - the PM writes the draft, the Workspace Owner publishes;
    - sub-items are allowed;
    - connection points are only for drawing lines;
    - each framework defines its own lanes.
  - If you believe a decision is wrong, say so plainly with the evidence and the consequences, but do not propose cutting scope because of team size.

# How to read the documents

1. Unzip the zip file with the code execution tool. List every file with its size. If you cannot open the zip, stop and tell me.
2. Read `round-2/metis-review-vong-2.md` and `round-2/review-disposition-round2.md` first.
3. Read the whole BRD addendum on onboarding, skipping no section. Then read the design spec, the option catalogue, the rulings and the three research notes, to understand the reason for each choice.
4. Read the whole BRD 4.4, part by part, to the end. Read closely sections 1.8, 1.9, 4.5, 5.2, 7.4 and 7.9; modules M02 to M05 and M08; sections 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20 and 21.
5. View all the images in `png/` (open and display the images to see the layout), especially the 12 onboarding screens 46 to 57 and screen 58; view `style-guide.png`. Use `wireframes-digest.md` to read the small text exactly.
6. If you cannot view the images, state this clearly at the top of the report, assess the visual part from the digest, and attach the label [Limited visual assessment] to the remarks about layout.
7. After that, do part O first, then parts A to I.

# Tasks

## O. Focus: the onboarding design (BRD addendum and wireframes 46 to 57)

The product owner's goal (section 4.1 of the BRD addendum): every customer can set up its company within 30 minutes of the main setup person's effort, reaching the "aha moment". That moment consists of:

- the workspace is active with a real project lifecycle;
- real people are invited;
- the existing projects have entered the portfolio;
- the executive cockpit has real figures.

The journey is in section 6 (the steps in 6.1, the pre-filled part in 6.2, the three executive questions in 6.3, a 30-minute session in 6.5) and section 10 (questions, delegation, launch, effort budget in 10.7). Assess the design by four criteria: **easy to understand, friendly, scientifically grounded, appealing to users.**

- **O1. Walk through the journey like a real user (cognitive walkthrough).**
  - User roles:
    - the C-level executive as the main setup person;
    - the delegate (PMO or Workspace Owner);
    - the Tenant Admin who turns on AI;
    - the PM whose project is adopted;
    - provider staff who create the tenant and pre-fill the information.
  - For each screen in journey order, answer four questions:
    - does the user want to do exactly what needs to be done;
    - does the user see the correct action;
    - does the user understand that this action leads to the goal;
    - after the action, does the user see that they are making progress.
  - Estimate the time of each step for a mid-sized company (state the assumptions, use ranges) and the total against 30 minutes. Point out each place where users are likely to abandon, and why.
- **O2. Easy to understand.**
  - Text on screen: whether internal terms (workspace, lifecycle, portfolio, framework...) are explained at the right moment; whether the questions fit the spirit of "ask from the executive's point of view, no preset numbers".
  - Visual hierarchy: whether each screen has one clear main task; whether the user knows where they are, how much is left and what to do next.
  - For each hard-to-understand sentence: quote it verbatim, say why it is hard, propose a replacement sentence.
- **O3. Friendly.**
  - Cognitive load at each step: the number of decisions, fields and question cards. Check smart defaults; skip and come back; undo; autosave; resuming on another device or on a phone.
  - Hard situations: the AI misreads, a file cannot be read, data is missing or contradictory, the delegate does not respond, the connection is lost. Do the messages say how to fix it?
  - Accessibility: keyboard, screen reader, contrast, states shown with a shape and text. Cross-check against style guide 0.3 section 7a and rule BR-41 of the main BRD.
- **O4. Scientifically grounded.**
  - Cross-check each design choice against the principles already studied in research on behavior and experience, for example:
    - progressive disclosure, cognitive load, the default effect, Hick's law;
    - goal-gradient and the progress bar, endowed progress, peak-end;
    - time-to-value, Fogg's behavior model.

    For each principle, say whether the design applies it correctly, applies it wrongly or misses it, and the consequence. Cite the source when giving research figures; attach [Needs verification] when unsure.
  - Check each line of Appendix D (market evidence) against the notes in `onboarding/research/`: whether the source says exactly that; which lines need [Needs verification] attached; whether any important evidence was left out.
  - Success metrics (ONB-26 and section 19.2): activation, time-to-value, completion rate, abandonment rate by step, rate of AI use versus the no-AI path. Whether the BRD defines them fully and measurably; propose additions.
  - Propose a validation plan before and during the pilot: usability tests (number of people, user roles, tasks, pass criteria) and the A/B tests worth running.
- **O5. Appealing to users.**
  - Is the "aha" moment strong enough for a C-level executive? Does the user feel progress, achievement and trust (transparent AI, preview before applying, undo)?
  - The three framing questions (section 6.3): which should be replaced, and with what.
  - Compared with the best onboarding of similar products and of well-known SaaS products [Needs verification]: what Metis lacks to make an impression in the first five minutes.
  - Tone of voice and emotion: whether it creates pressure or a fear of being wrong, or makes the user want to go on.
- **O6. Scoring and redesign.**
  - A scoring table of the 12 onboarding screens by the four criteria (1 to 5), with the biggest problem of each screen and its severity (0 to 4).
  - For the three weakest screens: sketch a redesign option in words (layout, content, interactions), detailed enough to redraw the wireframe.
  - Ten onboarding improvements ranked by their effect on the completion rate within 30 minutes.

## A. Closure check of round 2 items

- A table with all 24 rows, RF2-01 to RF2-24, with the columns:

## B. Process framework editor

- BLD-13 to BLD-16: whether the acceptance criteria can be verified. Cross-check for contradictions with:
  - BLD-03 to BLD-12, D-07, D-09;
  - GOV-17 to GOV-23, GOV-28;
  - BR-15, BR-16, BR-31, BR-41;
  - WBS-02, WBS-13, WBS-15;
  - section 14 and section 15.1.
- The publish path without review in Release 1, versions and provenance (BLD-10), deprecation against GOV-28: whether they are sound.
- The person in charge recorded by role or job title (WSP-10) and then assigned a person at build: whether this is feasible and easy to understand.
- Three wireframes `58-process-framework-editor`, `13-template-library`, `36-workspace-setup`:
  - whether they show the behavior correctly;
  - whether a user can author a framework without guidance;
  - whether keyboard operation and List mode are equivalent to the canvas.
- Cross-check against `poc-frameworks/poc-frameworks-coverage.md`: whether the BRD still misses any function of the POC's Frameworks menu.

## C. BRD addendum: requirements quality, architecture and security

- **ONB requirements:**
  - which acceptance criteria cannot be verified; ambiguities; missing requirements; overlaps;
  - whether the split into 27 P0 and 13 P1 is reasonable by value and risk (team size not considered);
  - whether the 8 rules BR-43 to BR-50 contradict BRD 4.4.
- **Architecture:**
  - using the Draft workspace as the draft (section 9.2);
  - the MCP setup tool group (section 7.1);
  - one pipeline for both Metis's AI and the customer's own AI (sections 9.5 and 12);
  - the no-AI path (section 9.6).
- **Security** per the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 (section 11):
  - remaining vulnerabilities;
  - specific scenarios: indirect prompt injection through documents the customer uploads, probing another customer's data, abusing tools, burning cost;
  - proposed controls.
- **Data and legal:** customer consent, data masking, sub-processors, Article 50 of the EU AI Act, file retention. Attach [Needs verification] to every legal point you are unsure about.
- **Examine closely the five most gap-prone points of the design:**
  - the definition of "30 minutes of effort" of the main setup person (section 4.1);
  - governance when adopting in-flight projects: recording "completed before Metis" without creating an approval decision (section 9.3);
  - the volume of the attention queue that lands on the executive after launch;
  - granting roles to the invitees at launch;
  - personal data sent to the LLM provider.

## D. The two documents match each other

For each contradiction, record the two locations cross-checked and propose a fix. Hints (not limited to these):

- Section 13 of the BRD addendum (20 proposed amendments): whether the "Today in v4.4" column quotes BRD 4.4 correctly; whether any amendment collides with the new part of version 4.4 (section 1.9).
- The onboarding starting pack contains a process framework (ONB-27). Compared with the draft and publish lifecycle of BLD-16: what state the framework in the starting pack is in, and who publishes it.
- The MCP setup tool group against BR-35, MCP-08, MCP-19 and MCP-20.
- The roles in section 14 of the main BRD against the roles in onboarding.
- WSP-14 and the screen `36-workspace-setup` against the onboarding journey.
- The ID scheme: duplicate IDs, reserved ID ranges, cross-references; the terms in Appendix A of the two documents.
- Sample data: Acme Holdings in the main BRD; Nova Energy and Kite Logistics in onboarding. Whether tenants, users and dates are consistent.

## E. Final pre-feasibility

- **E1. Scorecard:** A1 to A7 as in the previous two rounds. Each row has the round 1, round 2 and round 3 scores and the reason for the change.
- **E2. Scope and roadmap under A-07:**
  - whether the new parts (the editor in the Deliverable Builder workstream; the "Onboarding and intake" workstream in section 16 of the BRD addendum) are reasonably placed in milestones 1A, 1B;
  - new dependencies between workstreams;
  - estimate the time as ranges, state the assumptions clearly, attach the label "estimate".
- **E3. Final conclusion:** choose one of three: Go, Go with conditions, Not yet advisable. List the conditions for locking the baseline. Confirm or adjust the order of the decisions to settle first, including D-32 to D-39.

## F. Wireframe

- **F1. Coverage:** from `manifest.json`, confirm that every P0 requirement of both documents has a screen. List the P0 requirements whose screen only lists the ID but does not really show the behavior, with the file name.
- **F2. New screens and revised screens** (46 to 58, 13, 36): a table with the file name, whether the purpose is clear (1 to 5), the main problem, the proposed fix. For 46 to 57, refer to part O instead of repeating.
- **F3. Consistency across all wireframes:** terms, the "Planned" label, save state, data freshness, AI attribution, the keyboard focus loop. Judge only consistency, not the correctness of the fictional data.
- **F4. Accessibility:** cross-check style guide 0.3 and BR-41 against the table, tree, board, canvas and dialog screens.

## G. Friendliness of the other journeys

- Walk through the journeys in section 7.9 of BRD 4.4 again, including "Workspace setup" (which now has a step for authoring a process framework). For each journey:
  - the steps by screen;
  - the estimated number of actions;
  - the remaining friction points;
  - a proposal to shorten it.
- Nielsen's ten heuristics: report only findings that are new or still present outside part O. Each finding has a location (file name), the principle, a severity of 0 to 4, and a proposal.

## H. Round 3 refinement requests

- A table with the columns: ID (RF3-01, RF3-02…), Subject, Problem, Evidence, Specific proposed fix, Priority, Effort (S, M, L), Related (RF2-nn, RF-nn or "New").
- Priority has three levels: **Must before the baseline is locked**, **Should during Discovery**, **Could**. Because this is the last round, mark Must only for what truly blocks locking.
- Divide into four groups: Onboarding (BRD addendum and wireframes 46 to 57), Main BRD, Other wireframes, Style guide. Sort by priority. Include only new items or items not yet closed.

## I. Remaining questions for the client

Only the questions not already in D-01 to D-39 and Q-01 to Q-18, or those that the parts above show need to be asked again.

# Rules

- Follow constraint A-07 and the product owner's decisions in the Context section.
- Every finding points to evidence: a section number or ID in one of the two documents (for example BLD-16, ONB-15, BR-47, D-32), or a wireframe file name (for example `48-onboarding-draft-cockpit`).
- Separate the two kinds clearly: "Observation from the documents" and "Industry knowledge". Attach [Needs verification] to all market information, prices, legal points and research figures that you are not sure about.
- Do not invent figures. When estimating, state the assumptions and use ranges.
- The data in the wireframes is fictional sample data and the wireframes are mid-fidelity: do not score final aesthetics. Only part O is assessed for how appealing the layout, content and flow are.
- When the status is "Partly closed" or "Not closed", say exactly what is still missing and where.
- Do not propose starting over from scratch; every proposal must be achievable.
- Write in Vietnamese, with short, active sentences; keep the English terms and requirement IDs as they are.

# Output

A single Markdown file named `metis-review-vong-3.md`, created as a downloadable file. If you cannot create the file, print the whole content in one markdown block. Structure:

1. Executive summary:
   - the final conclusion;
   - a short assessment of onboarding by the four criteria;
   - the number of round 2 items that are closed, partly closed, not closed, or where a new defect arose;
   - the five things to do before the baseline is locked;
   - the five remaining risks.
2. Onboarding design (part O, O1 to O6).
3. Scorecard comparing the three rounds (E1).
4. Closure check of round 2 items (part A).
5. Process framework editor (part B).
6. BRD addendum: requirements, architecture, security (part C).
7. The two documents match each other (part D).
8. Final pre-feasibility (E2, E3).
9. Wireframes (part F).
10. The other journeys (part G).
11. Round 3 refinement requests (part H).
12. Questions for the client (part I).
13. Appendix: files read, assumptions, the list of [Needs verification] points.

If the content is too long for one reply, create the file in parts and then join them; do not shorten part O, the table in part A and the table in part H.
